lines: Morning, cháu. Pinewatch is yours now.
Tonight the board fills — seat them well and the stars follow.
I put the crew on the old warden's hut.
Watch the clock — a keepsake waits in every stage.
Rain tomorrow, the board says. A tarp keeps the reviews dry.
And cháu — the kettle's on if the morning runs long.
The fire smells of pine resin. Home, then.
Five stars last night, cháu. I saw the reviews.
Grandpa would have framed the log for that one.
Slept through the whole storm, I hope. Tarps earn their keep.
Wet nights make the best steam for morning tea, at least.
Someone got exactly what they were craving last night.
Grandpa always said a full pot reads the camp better than any review.
Whisper River. The fishing spot Grandpa swore by.
The bank seats closer to the water — anglers will want those.
First night on the river. Different water, same kettle.
Grandpa fished this bank for thirty years. Watch the anglers.
Tết Eve tonight, cháu — the river camps celebrate it.
Families will come. If the pantry can do bánh chưng, cook it.
Everyone stayed for the midnight pour. Tết done right.
Grandpa never missed one on this river. He'd be pleased, cháu.
Old Ba again. He fishes the same spot Grandpa did.
Three visits and he'll tell you the story of the koi.
River fog this morning — the rain kept the bank empty.
Guests still wrote warm things. The river forgives.
Lantern Valley — the last stop on Grandpa's map.
The photographers come for the light. Shelter them well.
Lantern Valley. The end of the road Grandpa drew.
Whatever he was walking toward — it ends here, or it doesn't.
Mid-Autumn tonight — the valley lights its lanterns.
Mooncakes in the pantry if you can make them. Photographers
will want the long exposure — keep the lanterns lit.
The lanterns went up one by one. I cried a little, cháu.
This is what Grandpa was building toward. The whole arc.
Lan again. She photographs the same bend every visit.
Patient one. Grandpa wrote about her family in the margins.
That was a proper mountain storm. Everyone under cover?
Grandpa's notes say the valley floods in old memories too.
Hùng again. Third stay, and he still checks the ridge first.
Whatever he's scouting for — Grandpa knew. The pennant waits.
Tonight we remember him. Every year, same riverbank.
Cook chè trôi nước if the pantry allows — it was his
offering food. Mostly, just keep the fire high.
The lantern went out on its own, near morning.
The book feels lighter. Grandpa's camp is ours now.
A familiar face on the board this morning.
They came back. Grandpa was right — the camp keeps people.
Someone from last week is back on the bank.
The river's starting to keep its own regulars.
A familiar tripod by the lanterns again.
Return visits are the valley's way of saying yes.
Three days of rain. The pads hold — Grandpa raised them right.
The guests are mud to the knees and smiling about it.
The river's up again, cháu. Third day — the bank camps
know what it means. Keep the dry pads for the latecomers.
Three clear nights running. The valley never shows off
like this twice — the camera earns its keep this week.
